PRELIMINARY LEGAL ASSESSMENT FOR REUSE OF MUNICIPAL DATA

This document analyzes the initial conditions for using Santa Marina City Council data and metadata in the SILEX project. It does not replace a decision by the legal office and does not itself grant authorization. Its purpose is to identify pending decisions, minimum controls, and limits that must be reflected in planning, architecture, and publication.

The assessment distinguishes procedure metadata, case data, and personal data from the municipal register. These categories do not have the same risk or basis of use. It also distinguishes internal access, demonstration to selected users, transfer between organizations, and open publication.

1. Context

SILEX needs procedure information to construct mappings, validate the ontology, and test an API. Most fields are administrative descriptions: titles, units, channels, deadlines, and legal bases. However, some exports may contain contact names, technical identifiers, or references to individual cases.

The existence of a copy in a municipal system does not imply that it may be transferred to the university. Before a dataset is received, the decision maker, purpose, licence or authorization, fields, and retention period must be identified. Restrictions must travel with the data and appear in the manifest.

2. Principles

Applicable principles are purpose limitation, minimization, necessity, traceability, security, and transparency. The project will use the minimum data compatible with its objectives. Synthetic records or metadata without personal information will be used wherever possible.

Pending decisions will be represented as pending. An incomplete licence will not receive an optimistic interpretation. Authorization for an internal test will be limited to that environment and will not be extended to the demonstrator or publication.

3. Purpose and basis of use

The project may use municipal metadata to design and evaluate the model where a defined public or research purpose and authorization from the responsible entity exist. The purpose must be limited to the pilot and does not automatically justify later uses.

The decision must remain linked to its supporting source, date, and competent person or body. Where the condition changes, a new version will be created; the earlier situation will not be deleted where it is required to explain history.

3. Registration data

The municipal register contains personal data and must not be added to the open catalogue. Technical authorization for an internal test is not a redistribution licence. Only the minimum necessary data will be used in a restricted environment.

The decision must remain linked to its supporting source, date, and competent person or body. Where the condition changes, a new version will be created; the earlier situation will not be deleted where it is required to explain history.

3. Procedure metadata

Titles, descriptions, units, channels, and legal bases may form part of the product where their source and conditions permit. Names of individual contacts will be excluded unless necessary and expressly authorized.

The decision must remain linked to its supporting source, date, and competent person or body. Where the condition changes, a new version will be created; the earlier situation will not be deleted where it is required to explain history.

3. Legal versions

Superseded rules must be retained for historical questions but not presented as current. The technical modification date of a file does not replace its legal validity period.

The decision must remain linked to its supporting source, date, and competent person or body. Where the condition changes, a new version will be created; the earlier situation will not be deleted where it is required to explain history.

3. Publication and demonstration

The public demonstrator will use only authorized data. A dataset available to the team may still remain outside a public interface. Publication must state licence, provenance, and limitations.

The decision must remain linked to its supporting source, date, and competent person or body. Where the condition changes, a new version will be created; the earlier situation will not be deleted where it is required to explain history.

3. Transfer to the municipality

Final transfer will include authorized software, models, catalogues, and documentation. Copies of restricted data and technical secrets will not be transferred outside the defined spaces.

The decision must remain linked to its supporting source, date, and competent person or body. Where the condition changes, a new version will be created; the earlier situation will not be deleted where it is required to explain history.

3. Retention

Working copies will be retained for the period needed for validation and auditing. They will then be deleted or archived according to dataset classification. Indefinite retention requires a specific purpose and policy.

The decision must remain linked to its supporting source, date, and competent person or body. Where the condition changes, a new version will be created; the earlier situation will not be deleted where it is required to explain history.

3. Responsibilities

Santa Marina makes decisions concerning municipal data and confirms licences and restrictions. UPSC applies technical controls, documents transformations, and reports incidents. Neither party may unilaterally expand the purpose.

The decision must remain linked to its supporting source, date, and competent person or body. Where the condition changes, a new version will be created; the earlier situation will not be deleted where it is required to explain history.

4. Specific assessment of registration data

The municipal register supports proof of residence and contains personal information. The SILEX catalogue does not need to copy individual records. It is sufficient to describe the registration-certificate procedure, requirements, unit, channel, and deadline. The preferred option is therefore to exclude register content from the semantic product.

If an internal test needs to check a connection to the system, it must use a controlled environment, a minimum sample, or synthetic data. Access will be limited to designated people, logs will not retain complete bodies, and the test will have an end date. Authorization must state whether a copy may be moved or only the municipal system may be queried.

Until the legal office issues formal confirmation, the dataset will be classified as restricted and awaiting a licence. This classification does not prevent the rest of the pilot from proceeding. The plan and deliverable must state that registration data is outside the public scope.

5. Metadata and legal bases

Procedure metadata may be published where it is public administrative information and contains no unnecessary personal data. Even so, provenance will be retained and the conditions of every export reviewed. Unit names will be accompanied by stable codes and validity periods.

Legal bases require version control. An earlier rule may be retained to answer historical questions, but the interface must prioritize the current rule when a query contains no date. The system will not use a file modification date as a substitute for legal validity.

6. Use matrix

Internal development: permitted for authorized metadata and synthetic data; restricted data requires specific authorization. Testing with municipal staff: permitted in a controlled environment using agreed datasets. Public demonstration: limited to authorized metadata and examples. Open publication: requires an explicit licence and final review. International transfer: outside scope unless separately assessed.

7.C1 — Source inventory

Maintain identifier, owner, licence, purpose, location, and responsible person.

The control must have an owner, execution frequency or date, and evidence. A policy without technical implementation or an operational record will not be sufficient to authorize a higher-risk use.

7.C2 — Classification

Mark every dataset as open, internal, restricted, or pending.

The control must have an owner, execution frequency or date, and evidence. A policy without technical implementation or an operational record will not be sufficient to authorize a higher-risk use.

7.C3 — Minimization

Extract only fields necessary for the test or product.

The control must have an owner, execution frequency or date, and evidence. A policy without technical implementation or an operational record will not be sufficient to authorize a higher-risk use.

7.C4 — Access

Use named accounts, least privilege, and periodic review.

The control must have an owner, execution frequency or date, and evidence. A policy without technical implementation or an operational record will not be sufficient to authorize a higher-risk use.

7.C5 — Traceability

Retain manifests, versions, transformations, and validation results.

The control must have an owner, execution frequency or date, and evidence. A policy without technical implementation or an operational record will not be sufficient to authorize a higher-risk use.

7.C6 — Publication

Run an automated check and human licence review.

The control must have an owner, execution frequency or date, and evidence. A policy without technical implementation or an operational record will not be sufficient to authorize a higher-risk use.

7.C7 — Environment separation

Do not mix restricted data with the public demonstrator.

The control must have an owner, execution frequency or date, and evidence. A policy without technical implementation or an operational record will not be sufficient to authorize a higher-risk use.

7.C8 — Incidents

Report loss, improper access, or erroneous publication and retain evidence.

The control must have an owner, execution frequency or date, and evidence. A policy without technical implementation or an operational record will not be sufficient to authorize a higher-risk use.

7.C9 — Deletion

Verify deletion of temporary copies and revoke access at the end.

The control must have an owner, execution frequency or date, and evidence. A policy without technical implementation or an operational record will not be sufficient to authorize a higher-risk use.

7.C10 — Change of purpose

Request a new assessment before using data for a different objective.

The control must have an owner, execution frequency or date, and evidence. A policy without technical implementation or an operational record will not be sufficient to authorize a higher-risk use.

8. Incidents and changes

Any unexpected access, loss, erroneous publication, or use for a different purpose will be reported to the municipal owner and UPSC privacy functions. Affected processing will stop, secure traces will be retained, and scope, cause, and correction will be documented.

A change in scope, participant, dataset, technology, or purpose may require a new assessment. Urgent changes may be applied to reduce risk, but expansion of use will never be presumed from silence.

9. Recommendations

First, continue the pilot using procedure metadata and synthetic data while the registration-data licence is resolved. Second, add legal classification to every load manifest. Third, technically separate internal and public environments. Fourth, make licence review a release criterion. Fifth, preserve the history of legal versions.

Sixth, identify in the transfer record which products are delivered and which remain restricted. Seventh, delete temporary copies at the end. Eighth, train the team in purpose, minimization, and reporting. Ninth, review access periodically. Tenth, do not present provisional authorization as final.

10. Conclusion

SILEX can proceed without using personal content from the municipal register. The core of the pilot is based on administrative metadata and interoperability rules. Legal uncertainty must appear as an explicit restriction rather than be hidden by a technical decision.

Publication of the catalogue and final transfer require evidence of licence, provenance, validation, and access control. Formal confirmation from Santa Marina will be the determining document for any use of registration data beyond a limited internal test.

Annex A. Evidence required to authorize a load

Before a municipal dataset is loaded, the authorization record must precisely identify the source system, included fields, purpose, people with access, and destination environment. It must state whether authorization covers a copy, remote consultation, or synthetic data only. It must also set a review date and explain what will happen when the pilot ends. A generic reference to the project does not replace this information.

The person responsible for loading will check that the received file matches the authorization record. If additional fields appear, loading will stop until their treatment is confirmed. The manifest will record the result of this check, the file checksum, and any filtering performed before storage. Pending datasets will remain separate from authorized datasets so that an automated task cannot include them in a publication.

Annex B. Pre-publication review criteria

The pre-publication review must answer five questions: whether the dataset has a sufficient licence, whether it contains only necessary fields, whether versions and validity periods are correct, whether unnecessary personal data has been removed, and whether provenance explains every value. The answers must be documented by both a technical reviewer and a person responsible for licences or privacy.

Where a record combines sources with different conditions, the most restrictive condition will apply to the combined product unless the parts can be separated verifiably. Licence errors are blocking even where the record has passed technical tests. The final package will contain an exclusion list with reasons so that absence of a dataset is not interpreted as an ingestion failure.
